title: Cache hit-rate dashboards (KV/prefix cache telemetry v2) — requirements + layout
author: Sergio Costa
body:
## 1. Purpose
This page defines the dashboard set for KV/prefix cache telemetry v2. The goal is a consistent, trustworthy view of cache effectiveness across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, with drilldowns that enable:
- Platform + Runtime to validate instrumentation and detect regressions.
- SRE to alert on meaningful hit-rate drops without excessive noise.
- Optimize to derive and explain “increase hit-rate” recommendations using the same definitions users see in Console.

This document is dashboard requirements + layout only. Metric and tag definitions are owned by the v2 spec (see related pages).

## 2. Audience
- Primary: Platform Observability, Telemetry/Analytics, SRE.
- Secondary: Runtime serving team, Optimize/Console.

## 3. Non-goals
- Designing customer-facing UI polish (beyond matching key labels and definitions).
- Replacing existing cost/latency dashboards; this is cache-focused.
- Introducing per-request or high-cardinality dimensions in dashboards.

## 4. Data prerequisites (must be true for dashboards to be considered correct)
Dashboards assume telemetry v2 metrics are present and stable:
- Cache outcome classification is emitted consistently (hit/miss/partial/uncacheable/error).
- Gateway/control-plane attribution fields are attached (deployment_mode, region, route/model identifiers) using the approved cardinality budget.
- Aggregation rules are applied upstream (e.g., route_group, model_family/model_id normalization, hashed tenant fields where applicable).

If these prerequisites are not met, use the data quality runbook rather than “fixing” dashboards to compensate.

## 5. Key definitions (display these as dashboard help text)
All dashboard panels must include a short “Definition” subtitle using the language below to avoid teams computing different hit-rates.

### 5.1 Cacheable prompt
A request is considered cacheable if it meets runtime cache eligibility checks (e.g., prefix length >= min_prefix_tokens, cache enabled, supported model/version, not excluded by policy). This is surfaced as:
- outcome = uncacheable for requests failing eligibility.

### 5.2 Hit, miss, partial
- hit: prefix/KV cache served the full eligible prefix for the request.
- partial: cache served some (but not all) of the eligible prefix. Typical causes include partial-prefill behavior, streaming retry boundaries, or policy truncation.
- miss: eligible but no usable cached prefix found.

### 5.3 Hit-rate (requests)
Hit-rate (requests) is computed only over cache-eligible traffic:
(hit_requests) / (hit_requests + miss_requests + partial_requests)

### 5.4 Hit-rate (bytes)
Hit-rate (bytes) reflects how much prefill compute is avoided:
(hit_bytes) / (hit_bytes + miss_bytes + partial_miss_bytes)

Note: partial requests contribute to both hit and miss byte counters. Panels must label this clearly.

### 5.5 Saved prefill time
saved_prefill_ms is an estimate of end-to-end prefill time avoided by cache reuse (post-instrumentation v2). It is an estimate, not an SLO.

### 5.6 Cacheable prompt ratio
cacheable_prompt_ratio = (cache_eligible_requests) / (total_requests)
This measures “how much of the workload could ever benefit from cache.” It is not a hit-rate.

## 6. Global dashboard set (Grafana folder: Platform → Cache Telemetry v2)
The v2 dashboards consist of 4 primary dashboards and 1 “Data Quality” companion.

### 6.1 Dashboard A — Executive overview (Global)
Name: “KV Cache — Overview (v2)”
Default time range: Last 6 hours (quick troubleshooting), with quick links for 24h/7d.

#### Variables (templating)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private | all
- region: all + top regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc.)
- model_family: all (grouped; avoid per-version by default)
- route_group: all (aggregated route identifier)
- tenant_scope: all | top_tenants (uses hashed/aggregated tenant bucket; no raw tenant_id)

Cardinality guardrails:
- Variables must default to “all” and only expand to approved aggregated tags.
- No request_id, prompt_hash, or raw tenant_id in any dashboard query.

#### Panels (top to bottom)
1) KPI tiles (single stat)
- Hit-rate (requests), eligible traffic only
- Hit-rate (bytes)
- Saved prefill time (sum, ms) + Saved prefill time (per 1k requests)
- Cacheable prompt ratio

2) Trend: Hit-rate (requests) over time
- Lines: overall + split by deployment_mode (3 lines max)
- Tooltip shows eligible request volume to disambiguate mix changes.

3) Trend: Hit-rate (bytes) over time
- Same split as above.

4) Trend: Saved prefill ms over time
- Two views in a single panel using dual axis or separate panels:
  a) sum(saved_prefill_ms)
  b) saved_prefill_ms per 1k eligible requests

5) Breakdown bar chart: Top route_groups by eligible volume (last 1h)
- Purpose: show where cache matters right now.
- Click-through drilldown to Dashboard B filtered to the selected route_group.

6) Breakdown bar chart: Top route_groups by lowest hit-rate (min eligible volume threshold)
- Apply a guard: only include route_groups with eligible_requests >= N (default N=500 in window) to avoid noise.

7) Breakdown: Cache outcomes share
- Stacked area or stacked bar over time: hit / partial / miss / uncacheable / error.
- This panel is the first check for “hit-rate dropped due to eligibility change” vs “true miss increase.”

#### “What changed?” link
Include a dashboard link (top-right) to:
- Runtime release notes dashboard annotation source (runtime train + deployment events)
- Feature-flag events for cache telemetry v2 enablement

### 6.2 Dashboard B — Route drilldown (Per-route / Per-tenant safe)
Name: “KV Cache — Route Drilldown (v2)”
Intended use: identify route-level offenders and fragmentation patterns.

#### Required filters
- route_group (required; default = top 20 by eligible volume)
- deployment_mode (default = all)

#### Panels
1) Hit-rate (requests) + eligible request volume (two-axis)
2) Hit-rate (bytes)
3) Saved prefill ms (sum and per 1k eligible requests)
4) Cacheable prompt ratio (route-level)
5) Model fragmentation table (within route)
- Columns: model_family, model_id (normalized), eligible_requests, hit_rate_requests, hit_rate_bytes
- Sorting: by eligible_requests desc
- Note: do not include model_version unless explicitly toggled via an “Advanced” variable (off by default).

6) Region fragmentation table (within route)
- Columns: region, eligible_requests, hit_rate_requests

7) Deployment-mode comparison
- Small multiples: hosted vs dedicated vs private (if present)

8) Error rate panel (cache telemetry errors)
- Show outcome=error as a share of total requests.
- Include a link to data quality runbook section “Missing/invalid cache outcome.”

### 6.3 Dashboard C — Capacity/efficiency view (Saved work)
Name: “KV Cache — Efficiency (v2)”
Intended use: correlate cache to latency/cost proxies and identify whether “high hit-rate” is actually producing savings.

Panels
1) Saved prefill ms (sum) by route_group (top N)
2) Saved prefill ms per 1k requests by route_group
3) Hit-bytes (sum) by route_group
4) Scatter: hit-rate (bytes) vs saved_prefill_ms per 1k eligible requests
- Each point: route_group (top 50 by eligible volume)
- Purpose: catch misclassification/estimation issues (e.g., high hit-rate but no savings)

5) Partial-prefill share
- partial_requests / eligible_requests by route_group
- Highlight top outliers; link to known issues page.

6) “Latency context” (optional; if base latency metrics available)
- Prefill latency p95 (non-cached) vs effective prefill time saved (estimate)
- This is explicitly labeled “context only” to avoid conflating with SLO.

### 6.4 Dashboard D — Deployment mode comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Name: “KV Cache — Deployments (v2)”
Intended use: ensure we can compare modes without broken attribution.

Panels
1) Eligible traffic volume by deployment_mode
2) Hit-rate (requests) by deployment_mode
3) Hit-rate (bytes) by deployment_mode
4) Cacheable prompt ratio by deployment_mode
5) Top regions per deployment_mode (table)
- For each deployment_mode: region, eligible_requests, hit_rate_requests

### 6.5 Companion — Data Quality & Cardinality
Name: “KV Cache — Data Quality (v2)”
Owned jointly by Telemetry + SRE; required for oncall.

Panels
1) Ingestion volume (cache metrics) vs request volume
- Detect missing emission or pipeline drops.

2) Sampling rate visibility (where applicable)
- If sampled: show effective sample rate by deployment_mode/region.

3) Cardinality watchdog
- Unique series count for cache metric families; alert if exceeding budget.
- Top offending tags (approximate), based on telemetry pipeline reports.

4) Unknown tag values / “other” bucket rate
- Percent of series aggregated into “other” due to guardrails.

5) Backfill lag / dataset freshness (if dashboards depend on aggregated datasets)

## 7. Required metrics & suggested query patterns
Note: exact metric names come from the v2 metric spec. The patterns below reflect how dashboards should compute derived values.

### 7.1 Derived metrics (dashboard-side)
All derived rates must:
- Use eligible traffic as denominator.
- Apply the same filters to numerator and denominator.
- Use consistent rollups (e.g., rate/sum over the same window).

Suggested derived expressions (pseudo-PromQL):
- eligible_requests = sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{outcome=~"hit|miss|partial"}[5m]))
- hit_rate_requests = sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{outcome="hit"}[5m])) / eligible_requests
- cacheable_prompt_ratio = sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{outcome=~"hit|miss|partial"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
- hit_rate_bytes = sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_bytes_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_bytes_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_bytes_total[5m])))
- saved_prefill_ms_per_1k = (sum(rate(kv_cache_saved_prefill_ms_total[5m])) / eligible_requests) * 1000

### 7.2 Normalization / grouping
- Prefer route_group over raw route_id.
- Prefer model_family or normalized model_id over model_version.
- Use deployment_mode and region as primary drilldowns.

## 8. Drilldown behavior (must be consistent across dashboards)
- From Overview → click route_group bar → opens Route Drilldown with route_group preselected.
- From Route Drilldown → click model row → opens Route Drilldown with model_id filter set (advanced).
- From any dashboard → “Data Quality” link preserves current filters (deployment_mode/region) to speed diagnosis.

## 9. Dashboard annotations (events overlay)
Dashboards must support annotations for:
- Runtime train deployments (runtime_version)
- Cache telemetry v2 feature flags enable/disable (flag name + scope)
- Control plane changes that affect attribution (gateway release)

Minimum requirement: a shared annotation source that can overlay on all four dashboards.

## 10. Acceptance criteria
Dashboards are considered ready for staged rollout when:
1) Definitions are consistent with v2 spec and displayed on dashboards.
2) Overview dashboard numbers match offline validation within agreed tolerance:
- Hit-rate (requests) within ±1.0 percentage point for a synthetic validation route.
- Saved prefill ms within ±10% for the same test, acknowledging estimation.
3) Drilldowns do not exceed cardinality limits (confirmed via Data Quality dashboard).
4) Panels render in <5 seconds p95 for last 6h at default filters.
5) SRE confirms the dashboard is sufficient to support regression alert triage.

## 11. Ownership and change process
- Dashboard owner: Sergio Costa (Eng Platform Observability)
- Data definitions owner: Logan Wright (Telemetry)
- Oncall/alertability reviewer: Sean Gallagher (SRE)

Changes to:
- Metric names/tags → require update to v2 spec + ADR if cardinality changes.
- Dashboard queries/derived math → PR to observability-pack (see related GitHub PR) with review by Telemetry + SRE.

## 12. Open questions (tracked in ENG-4817)
1) Should “partial” be included in eligible denominator for hit-rate (requests) for all views, or should we show two hit-rates (strict vs inclusive)? Current requirement: include partial in eligible denominator and show partial share separately.
2) Do we need a separate panel for “routing/pinning fragmentation score” once recommendation generator v0 is live? Proposal: add as a beta panel in Route Drilldown after v0 ships.
3) Private deployments: confirm which tags are always present (some Private gateways may not emit route_group). If missing, dashboards must gracefully fall back to “unknown_route_group” and surface this in Data Quality.

## 13. Appendix: Panel naming conventions
To keep Console/Optimize wording aligned, use these exact panel titles:
- “Hit-rate (requests, eligible traffic)”
- “Hit-rate (bytes)”
- “Saved prefill time (ms)”
- “Cacheable prompt ratio”
- “Cache outcomes (hit/miss/partial/uncacheable/error)”

Avoid ambiguous titles like “Cache hit-rate” without qualifier.
